sop_title: SOP-01 NTRR Account Request / Data Access Permission Request
summary: This process covers how an investigator or data manager requests an NTRR account and data access privileges, from submitting a signed Data Access Request (DAR) through review, authorization, account creation and first login. It is run by the applicant, with the Institutional Business Official signing, NTRR Operations staff reviewing, the NTRR Data Access & Quality Committee (DAC) authorizing, and the NTRR Admin creating the account.

sections.title: NTRR overview
sections.reason: It describes the portal's purpose, who may request accounts and why the DAC verifies credentials, and contains no ordered actions.

sections.title: Prerequisites
sections.reason: It is a requirement list (a signed DAR PDF) with no sequence; it is reflected as a gate on the upload step (S6) and the signing step (S5).

sections.title: Procedure (overview)
sections.reason: This is an introductory statement of scope with no ordered actions; its 1-3 business day duration is captured in timing.

sections.title: Data Access Permission Request Initiation
sections.reason: Order matters: the DAR must be downloaded, completed, signed and uploaded before the required fields and privileges are entered and the request is submitted.

sections.section: Data Access Permission Request Review and Authorization
sections.title: Data Access Permission Request Review and Authorization
sections.reason: Order matters: Operations reviews before forwarding to the DAC, and the DAC authorizes before the Admin creates the account and sends notification.

sections.title: Account Validation
sections.reason: Order matters: the applicant waits for the approval email before returning to log in and access data.

sections.title: DAR FAQs
sections.reason: The FAQ items could be reordered without losing meaning, but they gate DAR completion (required sections, PI versus non-PI content, Business Official sign-off), so they are mapped as steps S3-S5 and decision D1.

sections.title: Data Submission
sections.reason: It defines the GUID, Data Dictionary and Data Repository modules, which is reorderable definitional content with no actions.

steps.action: Applicant goes to the NTRR website, logs in and selects 'Request a New Account'

steps.source_quote: login using your username and password. Then click the "Request a New Account" link.

steps.source_quote: All pertinent information under Recipient Information and Certifications is required.

steps.source_quote: Please be sure to include your Project Director/Principal Investigator Contact Information

steps.source_quote: The person who signs off on this section of the form needs to be responsible for assuring compliance

steps.output: DAR uploaded to the account request

steps.action: Applicant selects the Data Repository, Query and Datastore privileges and submits the request
steps.input: Completed account request with uploaded DAR
steps.output: Submitted account request; confirmation page displayed if all required fields were entered

exceptions.trigger: A new applicant has no username and password, but the SOP requires logging in before clicking 'Request a New Account'.
Required fields were not successfully entered, so no confirmation page is displayed.
Operations finds errors in the DAR; the SOP does not say how the applicant responds or resubmits, or whether review restarts.
exceptions.handling: The NTRR Operations team may contact the applicant for more information; nothing further is stated.
exceptions.source_section: Data Access Permission Request Review and Authorization

exceptions.trigger: The DAC does not authorize data access.
exceptions.source_section: Data Access Permission Request Review and Authorization

exceptions.trigger: The approval email is not received in a timely manner.
exceptions.handling: Check the spam filter and/or reach out to the NTRR team.

exceptions.trigger: The applicant contacts the NTRR team about a missing approval email; the resolution is not described.

timing.requirement: The entire procedure typically requires 1-3 business days, assuming the Prerequisites (signed DAR PDF) are already met.
The approval email is expected 'in a timely manner'; no specific wait time is defined before checking spam or contacting the NTRR team.

risks.description: Data Access Permission Request Initiation step 2 tells the applicant to log in with a username and password before clicking 'Request a New Account'. The SOP does not say how a new applicant without credentials gets them, so the entry point to the process has no defined path.

Initiation step 10 says a confirmation page appears only 'if all required fields were successfully entered'. D2's No branch has no stated next step, and the SOP gives no request ID or receipt, so the applicant cannot tell whether the request was received.

Review and Authorization step 2 says Operations 'may contact the applicant' when the DAR has errors. The SOP does not say how the applicant corrects or resubmits the DAR, whether review restarts at S9, or what happens if the applicant does not respond.
Contacting the applicant about errors is optional ('may contact'), and no timeframe is given. A DAR with errors could stall at Operations with no defined action.

Review and Authorization step 4 only describes the DAC authorizing access. There is no path for denial or partial authorization (D4 No branch is UNDEFINED), and nothing says the applicant is told of a rejection.
Operations staff 'provides this form to the NTRR DAC' (Review and Authorization step 3). The SOP names no channel, tracking or queue, so requests can sit between Operations and the committee unseen.

The Admin sets up a user account 'with the privileges corresponding to data access' based on DAC authorization (step 5). No recorded authorization is passed over, and nothing checks that the privileges granted match what the DAC approved. This matters because the data is confidential research-participant data.

The handoff of the DAC authorization to the NTRR Admin (between steps 4 and 5 of Review and Authorization) has no stated mechanism or record. Approved requests could wait for provisioning with no tracking.

Initiation step 8 tells every applicant to check the Data Repository, Query and Datastore privileges. DAR FAQs Q5 says 'You should request modules based on your need in the system' and also lists the Data Submission modules (GUID, Data Dictionary). The two sections give different rules for which privileges to request.

The applicant enters Recipient Information in the DAR PDF (S3, per DAR FAQs Q1). They then fill in required applicant fields again on the Account Management page (Initiation step 6). The same identity and contact data is entered twice, and Operations must check that the two match.

DAR FAQs Q4 says the authorized Business Official 'can vary from site to site'. Operations' review (S9) checks only 'accuracy and completeness', and no step verifies that the signer actually has authority to accept the data-use conditions.
The DAR passes from the applicant to the Business Official for signature and back, outside any system (DAR FAQs Q4, Prerequisites). This handoff has no tracking or timing.

No turnaround is set for the Operations review or the DAC review. Only a 'typically requires 1-3 business days' estimate for the whole procedure is given (Procedure), and it is unclear who in the committee acts.
Account Validation step 1 asks the applicant to escalate if the email does not arrive 'in a timely manner'. No wait time is defined before the applicant checks spam or contacts the team.
The applicant is told to 'reach out to the NTRR team', but the SOP gives no contact channel, owner or resolution for a missing approval email.

recommendations.label: eliminate
recommendations.reason: Once the DAR is captured as a web form (A2), there is no template to download.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Pages / Power Apps form replaces the downloadable template

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: Capturing Recipient Information and Certifications in a form with required-field validation enforces DAR FAQs Q1 at entry and creates a trackable record. Applicants are external researchers, so this likely needs a Power Pages portal rather than an internal canvas app.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Pages (external) or Power Apps form writing to a SharePoint 'DAR Requests' list

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: A conditional section that appears and becomes required only when the applicant answers 'No' to 'Are you the PI?' applies the PI versus non-PI rules in DAR FAQs Q2 and Q3 without relying on the applicant reading the FAQ.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps / Power Pages conditional visibility and required fields on the same DAR form

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: Routing the completed DAR to the Business Official for signature or approval replaces an untracked offline handoff. The sign-off decision itself stays with the Business Official.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with Approvals connector or an e-signature connector (Adobe Acrobat Sign / DocuSign, premium)

recommendations.label: eliminate
recommendations.reason: The signed DAR and signature record are stored automatically with the request (A4), so the applicant no longer needs to upload a signed PDF separately.
recommendations.suggested_tool: SharePoint list item with stored signed DAR attachment

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: Collecting the account fields and the description of interest in the same form as the DAR removes the duplicate entry flagged in R10.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps / Power Pages form writing to SharePoint

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: Privilege selection becomes a form field with the module options from DAR FAQs Q5. Submission creates a record with a request ID, which removes the undefined no-confirmation branch (R2). The conflicting privilege guidance (R9) needs a process-owner decision before the choice list is set.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps / Power Pages choice field writing to SharePoint

recommendations.label: ai_assist
recommendations.reason: An AI step can pre-check the DAR text for missing required sections, a missing PI contact section for non-PIs, and missing Business Official information, then summarize gaps for Operations. Operations staff still confirm accuracy.
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with AI Builder prompt (GPT) on the SharePoint DAR record

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: Sending a standard correction request, tracking the 'Returned to applicant' status and re-queuing the request on resubmission defines the missing resubmission path (R3) and adds timing (R4).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with SharePoint and Office 365 Outlook connectors

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: When Operations marks a DAR complete, the flow starts a tracked DAC approval and records the outcome. This replaces the untracked handoff (R6) and gives the Admin a recorded authorization (R7, R8).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with Approvals, SharePoint and Planner/Outlook connectors

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.reason: The DAC verifies professional credentials and decides access to confidential trauma-research participant data. This is a sensitive judgment that must stay with the committee.
recommendations.suggested_tool: None (DAC decision captured through the A10 approval)

recommendations.label: keep_human
recommendations.reason: Granting privileges on a restricted-access portal is access-control provisioning, and the NTRR website has no standard connector. The Admin keeps this step, working from the DAC-authorized privilege list supplied by the A10 flow.
recommendations.suggested_tool: None (Admin task created by the A10 flow)

recommendations.label: automate
recommendations.reason: Automatic status emails at each stage (submitted, returned, with DAC, authorized, not authorized), plus a reminder when a request exceeds a defined time, replace 'watch your inbox… in a timely manner' (R14).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Automate with SharePoint and Office 365 Outlook (shared mailbox) connectors

recommendations.label: digitize
recommendations.reason: A support request form routed to an Operations-owned list gives 'reach out to the NTRR team' a defined channel and owner (R15).
recommendations.suggested_tool: Power Apps / Power Pages form writing to a SharePoint 'NTRR Support' list

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint - When an item is created or modified in the 'DAR Requests' list (Status column changed), plus a separate daily Recurrence trigger for reminders
actions: Get the DAR Requests item and its previous Status value (trigger condition: Status changed)
Switch on Status: Submitted, Returned to applicant, With DAC, Authorized, Not authorized, Account created
Office 365 Outlook - Send an email from a shared mailbox to the applicant with the request ID and a status-specific template
Update the item: set 'Last notified' date and append to a notification log column
Recurrence flow: get items where Status is not 'Account created' and the created date is older than the process-owner-defined limit (the SOP gives only '1-3 business days typically')
For each overdue item, send a reminder email to the NTRR Operations shared mailbox

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint - When an item is modified in 'DAR Requests' where Review Outcome = 'Errors found' (set by Operations staff)
actions: Get the item and the Operations reviewer comments (and the A8 AI completeness summary, if available)
Compose a correction request listing the errors found
Update the item: Status = 'Returned to applicant', set 'Returned date'
Office 365 Outlook - Send an email to the applicant with the correction request and a link to edit the DAR record
Do until the applicant resubmits (Status = 'Resubmitted') or a process-owner-defined timeout passes
On resubmission: clear Review Outcome, set Status = 'Awaiting Operations review', notify the Operations shared mailbox
On timeout: notify Operations to follow up or close the request (closure rule to be defined by the process owner)

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint - When an item is modified in 'DAR Requests' where Review Outcome = 'Complete' (set by Operations staff)
actions: Get the item, the signed DAR attachment and the requested privileges
Update the item: Status = 'With DAC', set 'Sent to DAC date'
Start and wait for the DAC approval (see approval step)
Record the outcome, approver names, comments and date on the item
If approved: set Status = 'Authorized', store the authorized privilege list, and create a Planner task or send an email to the NTRR Admin to set up the account with exactly those privileges
If rejected: set Status = 'Not authorized' and notify Operations (the applicant communication for a denial is not defined in the SOP and needs a process-owner decision)
starter_flows.approval_step: Approvals - Start and wait for an approval assigned to NTRR DAC members, with the DAR link, the applicant's description of interest and the requested privileges. Whether one member or all members must approve is not stated in the SOP and must be confirmed by the process owner.
